keyVerseText: The one and twentieth to Jachin, the two and twentieth to Gamul,
rootMeaning: The root of גָּמוּל (gâmûwl) is גָּמַל (gâmal), which carries the fundamental idea of recompense, reward, or dealing bountifully. As a passive participle, גָּמוּל literally means 'rewarded' or 'weaned,' suggesting a state of having been fully dealt with or matured. This root sense enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing a process of completion or fulfillment, whether in nurturing (weaning) or in receiving due recompense.
usageInScripture: The word גָּמוּל appears only once in Scripture as a proper name, designating a chief of the Levites and leader of the 22nd course in the temple service. Its translation as 'to Gamul' in 1 Chronicles 24:17 reflects its use as a personal name rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence highlights its function as a title or identifier within the sacred liturgical context, rather than a descriptive term.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding גָּמוּל as 'rewarded' or 'weaned' draws attention to themes of divine provision and faithful service. The Levite Gamul, as a priestly leader, symbolizes those who have been nurtured and prepared for God’s work, reflecting the spiritual maturation believers undergo. The concept of recompense inherent in the root reminds Christians of God’s just and generous dealings with His people, rewarding faithfulness and service. This aligns with the biblical narrative of God’s covenantal faithfulness and the believer’s call to mature in holiness and ministry.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Chronicles 24:17, the phrase 'The one and twentieth to Jachin, the two and twentieth to Gamul' identifies Gamul as the head of the 22nd priestly division. The use of the name Gamul here conveys not just a leader’s title but also implicitly reflects the idea of one who is 'rewarded' or 'fully matured' for sacred service. This enriches the verse by underscoring the orderly and divinely appointed structure of temple ministry, where each leader, including Gamul, represents a stage of spiritual readiness and responsibility.
